dedupe_keys.name: global coastal loss and adaptation outputs from pyciam

description: Climate Impact Lab publishes this pyCIAM output collection to reproduce and reuse global coastal-loss estimates. The archive contains results under multiple sea-level-rise scenarios, a replication of the earlier Diaz model and intermediate storm-surge loss lookup tables. Inputs include socioeconomic projections through 2100 and local sea-level quantiles. Coastal regions follow the SLIIDERS segmentation, including intersections of approximately 50-kilometre segments and administrative units. A modeller can use the tables to compare adaptation costs or check coastal risk calculations without rerunning every scenario. Zenodo provides compressed Zarr products free under CC BY 4.0, with Python examples for reading them through xarray. The largest output is about 13 GB compressed, so storage requirements are substantial. A limitation is that these are conditional economic-model outputs, not observed disaster losses. Their assumptions should accompany any reuse. Existing data-ipcc-ar6-sea-level-projections supplies a related sea-level input family. The separate pyCIAM software draft records the model itself. No dataset files were downloaded.
